F001.text: Gale Crater is a giant bowl on Mars about 154 km (96 miles) wide!

F002.text: Mount Sharp is a huge mountain in the middle of Gale Crater, standing 5 km (3 miles) tall!

F003.text: NASA's Curiosity rover safely landed inside Gale Crater in August 2012.

F004.text: Mars has two tiny moons named Phobos and Deimos.

F005.text: Curiosity uses a weather station to measure how cold the Martian ground gets.

F006.text: Curiosity stays warm on cold nights using heat from its own special nuclear battery!

F007.text: In Gale Crater, Curiosity measured nighttime ground temperatures dropping to -72°C (-98°F).

F008.text: In 2018, a giant dust storm covered the entire planet of Mars!

F009.text: The 2018 storm blocked out the Sun, so the solar-powered Opportunity rover couldn't get enough energy.

F010.text: Martian dirt has a little bit of water trapped inside it—about two pints of water in every cubic foot of dirt!

F011.text: Because Mars is so far away, a message takes anywhere from 3 to 22 minutes to reach Earth.

F012.text: A message between Earth and Mars can take about 3 to 22 minutes to travel one way.

F013.text: Rovers have to drive themselves safely because remote control from Earth is too slow!

F014.text: NOAA and NASA scientists watch the Sun every single day to keep astronauts safe from space weather.

F015.text: Solar flares are rated by letters like C (small), M (medium), and X (giant!).

F016.text: Space weather sensors recorded a huge X5.1-class solar flare in November 2025!

F017.text: Curiosity has a special tool that has been measuring invisible space radiation since it landed.

F018.text: Just like Earth, Mars can have beautiful glowing auroras in the sky during solar storms!

F019.text: Mars rocks are sharp! Curiosity's wheels got little holes in them, so NASA had to drive it carefully.

F020.text: The International Space Station uses tools like a robotic sniffer to help find tiny leaks!

F021.text: Mars has very thin air, so small space rocks can easily reach the ground and make fresh craters!

F022.text: NASA is practicing on the Moon right now so humans can safely explore Mars in the future.
